# Let Apple Calendar write your meeting notes for you

**Hook:**
You finish a meeting, open Apple Calendar on your iPhone or Mac, and the AI has already drafted a clear summary with key points and action items. No typing, no copying, just tap to save or share. Perfect for busy professionals who want concise notes without the hassle.

---

## Before you start
- An **iPhone, iPad, or Mac** running iOS 18.1+, iPadOS 18.1+, or macOS Sequoia 15.1+ (or later).
- **Apple Intelligence** enabled in Settings → Apple Intelligence & Siri.
- At least one **Apple Calendar event** scheduled in the next day (so the AI has something to summarise).
- Total time: about **5 minutes** to set up and test.

> ⚠️ **Note:** This feature is part of Apple Intelligence and may require a compatible device and software version. It’s not available on all devices or regions.

---

## Step 1 — Open the Calendar event you want to summarise
On your **iPhone or iPad**, open the **Apple Calendar** app. Tap the meeting you want to summarise. On a **Mac**, open the Calendar app and double-click the event.

👉 You’ll see the event details: date, time, attendees, and a notes section.

After tapping the event, look for a new button or option that says something like **"Summarise"** or **"Generate Notes"** — it may appear under the event title or in a menu.

💬 Example:
Tap the event titled *"Team Sync – Q3 Planning"* in your calendar.

You'll know it worked when you see a prompt or button inviting you to generate a summary.

---

## Step 2 — Tap “Summarise” or “Generate Notes”
Once inside the event, look for a button or option that says **"Summarise"** or **"Generate Notes"** — it’s usually near the top, under the event title or in a menu that appears when you tap the event again.

👉 After tapping it, Apple Intelligence will process the meeting details and draft a short summary.

If you don’t see the button, try pulling down slightly on the event screen to refresh, or look for a **⋯ (ellipsis)** or **More** button — tap it to reveal more options.

💬 Example:
Tap “Summarise” in the event titled *"Client Call – Website Redesign"*.

You'll know it worked when the screen shows a new section with a heading like **"Meeting Summary"** and a few bullet points.

---

## Step 3 — Review the AI-generated summary
The AI will show a draft summary with key points, decisions, and action items. Read it carefully.

👉 You can edit the text directly if something is missing or incorrect — just tap into the summary box and make changes.

If the summary is too short or misses a key detail, tap **"Regenerate"** or **"Improve"** to ask the AI to try again with more context.

💬 Example:
You see:
> • Decided to launch the new homepage by 15 Nov
> • Sarah to draft copy by Friday
> • Budget approved at $8,500

You'll know it worked when you see a clear, readable summary with bullet points and action owners.

---

## Step 4 — Save or share the summary
Once you’re happy with the summary, you can:
- **Save it** by tapping **Done** or **Save** — it will stay in the event’s notes.
- **Copy it** by tapping and holding the text, then choosing **Copy**.
- **Share it** by tapping the **Share** button and sending it via Messages, Mail, or another app.

👉 On iPhone/iPad, the Share button looks like a square with an arrow pointing up. On Mac, it’s in the top-right corner of the summary box.

If you don’t see a Share button, make sure the summary is fully loaded — sometimes it appears after a second.

💬 Example:
Tap **Share**, then choose **Messages**, and send it to your team.

You'll know it worked when the summary is saved in the event or successfully shared.

---

## Step 5 — Turn on automatic summaries for future events (optional)
To save time, you can enable automatic summaries for all future events.

On your **iPhone or iPad**, go to **Settings → Calendar → Summaries**. Turn on **"Summarise Events"**.

👉 On a **Mac**, go to **Calendar → Settings → Advanced**, and look for **"Summarise Events"** — enable it there.

After enabling, new events will automatically include a summary when they end.

If you don’t see this option, your device or software may not support it yet — check for updates.

You'll know it worked when future events show a summary section without you having to tap anything.

---

## Common mistakes
- **Mistake:** You don’t see the “Summarise” button.
  ✅ **Fix:** Pull down gently on the event screen to refresh, or tap the **⋯ (ellipsis)** or **More** button to reveal hidden options.

- **Mistake:** The summary is too short or misses key points.
  ✅ **Fix:** Tap **Regenerate** or **Improve** to ask the AI to try again with more context from the event details.

- **Mistake:** You can’t find where the summary is saved.
  ✅ **Fix:** Open the event again — the summary appears in the **Notes** section at the bottom of the event details.

---

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:**
  After your next meeting, open Calendar and let Apple Intelligence turn your notes into a clean summary. Save it to the event or share it with your team in seconds — no extra apps or typing required.

- **For your business or work:**
  Use this to keep your team aligned without manual note-taking. Share summaries directly from Calendar via Messages or email, saving time in follow-ups and reducing miscommunication.

- **If you're just getting started:**
  Start with one meeting this week. Turn on automatic summaries, then review the result. Once you trust it, use it for every meeting — it’s like having a quiet assistant in your pocket.

---

## Try it now
Open Apple Calendar on your iPhone or Mac, tap any meeting today, and look for the **"Summarise"** button. Generate a summary, review it, and share it with a teammate in under two minutes.
